scenes.heading: Building case studies that make your pitch easier

sents.d: Building case studies that make your pitch easier
A specific before-and-after story sells better than a general claim about your results.

A case study — one real client, the problem they had, what you did, and the specific result — is far more persuasive in a pitch or on a landing page than a general statement like 'we get results,' because it's concrete and verifiable.

scenes.heading: Gather details right after a win

sents.d: Ask permission and gather the details (numbers, timeline, a quote) right after a project wraps successfully, while it's fresh and the client is happy — waiting months makes it harder to get a good quote or accurate numbers.

scenes.heading: One or two strong case studies

sents.d: Even one or two strong case studies, reused across your pitch deck, website, and proposals, do more for conversion than a long list of vague testimonials.

take: Capture real results right after a project and reuse them.
